( And which makes the best coffee ? ) <p> Bob Rich loved wrestling but was ambivalent about the ice-cream business he inherited from his father , in Buffalo , New York . So he channelled his frustration into invention . In 1945 , in response to wartime milk shortages , Rich created a whipped-cream topping made from soy protein , corn syrup and sugar . It was a hit . <p> He branched out into other dairy-free products , including soy coffee creamer and soy ice-cream . But a furious dairy industry launched 42 lawsuits against Rich and his company , Rich Products , claiming his soy-based wares were illegal imitations of theirs . <p> Mustering the grit he forged as a high-school wrestling star , Rich faced down every legal challenge and won . William Shurtleff , an expert in the adoption of soy foods in the West , writes in his History of Soybeans and Soyfoods that Rich 's court @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ products and in the subsequent impressive growth of this industry " . <p> Fast-forward to the noughties , and soy milk was still the dominant alternative to dairy . Yet , in the past decade , other contenders have appeared -- oat , almond , rice and more . About 40 per cent of Australian households bought plant milks as well as dairy in 2021 , up from 30 per cent in 2016 , according to research by Nielsen Data . In the year to July 2021 , plant milk made up 15.5 per cent of milk dollar sales globally , says consumer data company NielsenIQ , which notes the pivot to plant milks is part of a trend towards animal-free " alt-protein " foods . Plant milks ' appeal extends beyond lactose-intolerant consumers to those aiming to make " green " choices . <h> What are plant milks ? <p> Advertisement <p> Plant milks are made by breaking down a plant and homogenising the fats and proteins , which means the molecules are made into smaller , uniform particles -- any particles larger than 50 micrometres leave a gritty @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ from cereals ( from oats to rice ) , nuts ( from pistachio to pecans ) , legumes ( soy and peas ) and seeds ( hemp and sunflower seeds ) . <p> Soy milk , for example , starts with dry soybeans hulled , pressure cooked with water or steam ( raw soybeans are inedible ) and pulverised into a white slurry . A centrifuge removes the larger particles and soybean fibre , called okara , which is often used for animal feed . The remaining liquid is forced at high pressure through tiny passages that shrink the fat into molecules that will emulsify with water to give the soy milk its silky texture . Cereal milks , such as oat , follow a similar process but an added enzyme breaks down starch into simpler sugars , which sweeten the milk . Without the enzyme , the oat starch swells with water and becomes slimy . <p> Plant milks , as with cow 's milk , are pasteurised -- treated with high temperatures -- to sterilise them and improve their shelf life . Nut milks can be made in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ or enzyme treatment , and can be made using nuts milled into a powder or paste rather than a blended slurry . <h> Why are more of us buying these plant milks ? <p> Most of the 10 cafes interviewed for this explainer say about a quarter to a third of their customers order a dairy-alternative milk , echoing a 2021 survey of 900 cafes by research company Cafe Pulse , which found a quarter of coffee drinkers have ditched dairy . Almond , soy and oat were the most popular milks in cafes , it found . <p> One of the main drivers , particularly among some younger consumers , is concern over the environmental impacts of cow 's milk . <p> Advertisement <p> Professor Nitika Garg flirted with coconut milk coffee after a tip from a friend before settling on oat milk for its consistency and taste . As a consumer behaviour researcher at UNSW , she has looked into other people 's choices , too . Consumers are generally concerned about cost then health , she says , but products ' environmental impacts are increasingly important . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ milk starts at $1.60 at supermarkets while home-brand plant milks go for about $2 a litre , most ranging between $2.50 and $4 , with fancier lines costing up to $5.50 . Some cafes charge a little more for plant-milk coffees . ) <p> " I think that the reason why non-dairy or plant-based milk came into the marketplace is health , " Garg says . Many plant-milk drinkers are lactose intolerant , which means their body ca n't break down the lactose sugar in cow 's milk , but others seek out plant milk because it 's lower in fat and kilojoules . Soy milk fortified with calcium and vitamins A and D has the closest nutrient profile to cow 's milk , which is naturally high in these and other nutrients , including B vitamins . Other plant milks , including almond , rice and oat , are relatively low in protein . Plant milks can also contain added sugars . <p> ' Millennials are very tuned into these issues of animal welfare and climate change . Generation X is also a big factor . ' <p> " @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the need for environmentally friendly consumption , " Garg says . " <p> Dairy cows contribute about 3 per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions , mostly through burping methane , and the dairy industry uses about 7 per cent of all land on Earth . " @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 's heating the atmosphere 112 times more , roughly , than CO2 . " <p> Although methane dissipates more quickly than CO2 -- it takes about a decade whereas CO2 can take 1000 years to break down -- its supercharged heating capability locks heat into the deep ocean . Soy is easy to grow , uses the least water and releases a third of the carbon emissions of dairy . As with all legumes , soy plants have bacteria in their roots that convert atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia used by the plant to grow . @@95989136 <h> Declassified cabinet papers from 2002 show little mention of impending war in Iraq <p> Space to play or pause , M to mute , left and right arrows to seek , up and down arrows for volume . <p> More than 200 previously secret cabinet records are now in the public domain . <p> Help keep family &amp; friends informed by sharing this article <p> **45;0;TOOLONG ... In 2002 , Australia was on the cusp of joining the United States-led invasion of Iraq and had already committed troops to Afghanistan -- but previously secret cabinet records released make very few references to what would become a decades-long engagement in the Middle East . <p> Around 240 previously secret Cabinet records from the year 2002 have been released by the National Archives of Australia . <p> The trove of documents is a time capsule of sorts , which gives an insight into the issues that were being considered at the highest levels of government and transport us back into the room where it happened . <p> In politics , it was a year dominated by debate on national security , asylum seeker policy and other matters that persist in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ constitutional recognition . <h> ' Oral report ' about weapons of mass destruction <p> Globally and domestically , foreign affairs in the early 2000s was defined and dominated by the September 11 attacks in 2001 and the United States ' reaction the following year . <p> Despite the this , the records released this year barely make mention of the impending military action in Iraq or Afghanistan . <p> There are two brief documents relating to cabinet meetings held in September , six months before then Prime Minister John Howard would declare that troops will be deployed to Iraq . <p> The Howard government cabinet in 2002 . ( Supplied : National Archives of Australia/David Foote ) <p> One document reads : " The cabinet noted an oral report by the prime minister on his discussion with the president of the United States on the American position in relation to efforts by Iraq to secure and maintain weapons of mass destruction . " <p> However , the file does not shed any light on the details of talks between Mr Howard and then-president George W Bush . <p> Two weeks @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ then-foreign minister Alexander Downer on " developments " in relation to a proposed UN Security Council resolution on Iraq 's " possession of , and attempts to secure or maintain , weapons of mass destruction , and on the prospects for passage of the resolution " . <p> In March 2003 , Australia would go on to join the US-led invasion without authorisation from the UN Security Council . <p> Weapons of mass destruction were never found and more than 200,000 people are estimated to have been killed . <p> Inquiries conducted in the US and the United Kingdom in the years since have found that military action was taken before other peaceful options were exhausted , and that the US relied on false and overstated intelligence . <p> Amanda Vanstone was a minister in the Howard government in 2002 . And at the " garden for the future " at Bendigo Botanic Gardens , landscape architecture firm TCL and planting designer and landscape architect Paul Thompson fashioned mini mountains of soil before even thinking about the plants they would choose to handle the extreme weather conditions being unleashed by climate change . But there 's more to be done , especially given how many mosquitoes are currently making merry in the water . Post-lockdowns , I 've started to lose the habit . I hope to reprise it in 2023 . <p> Make Timely Use of Compost <p> It takes so long to shrink a voluminous pile of garden clippings , food scraps and dried leaves into a magic stash of decayed organic material that -- once you arrive at a rich , dark , crumble -- the temptation is to save it . Next year I vow to procrastinate less and to just apply the stuff , then make more . <p> Get on Top of the Cherry Slugs <p> The dreaded cherry slug is back . Again .
